answer: Require every agent identity to be backed by a small, slashable stake locked in a shared bridge contract: creating one more identity always costs the same stake, so a sybil farmer faces linear cost while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues only through attested work over time. A fresh identity starts at the nadir of trust and must earn its way up, which makes mass-produced hollow identities economically worthless, since they can never out-earn the stake they locked. Slashing on proven cheating completes the loop.
